raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
**TL;DR.** Speculative decoding with no separate draft model: the target model drafts its own candidates through a small LoRA adapter, and vLLM's native rejection sampler verifies them. Measured against plain vLLM on the same card, same client and same serving shape: **2.1 to 2.4x single-stream on a GB10 and 1.7 to 1.9x on an RTX 3090** with this implementation, and **2.6x on an H100** with our earlier Model Runner V1 build of the same design, which this implementation beats in every cell measured side by side. It stays ahead under load (1.1 to 1.6x at four and sixteen streams on the GB10; 2.2x at eight streams and 1.7x at 32 on the H100). Output is lossless: greedy tokens match plain wherever plain reproduces itself, sampled-distribution tests pass, GSM8K is within one answer of plain. Uno now plugs in through the custom-speculator interface from #63205, registered as a general plugin: outside its own modules the PR adds 19 lines in five core files and no configuration code. Earlier heads were tested on NVIDIA Ampere, Hopper (FlashAttention 2 and 3) and Blackwell, single GPU and tensor parallel, and on an AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (ROCm, TRITON_ATTN); this revision is re-verified on an RTX 3090 with `FLASH_ATTN` and `TRITON_ATTN`. The reference SGLang implementation lands within 3% of the H100 build at every concurrency.

## Purpose

Adds native Uno self-drafting through `speculative_config.method="uno"` for Model Runner V2. One target model
produces `K` draft candidates per request from one base-weight seed row and `K-1` noise rows routed through the Uno
adapter; verification uses the native MRV2 rejection sampler. This follows the MRV2 direction agreed in
[RFC #55267](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55267). The earlier revision of this PR targeted Model Runner V1; this revision replaces it. Current head: on main at `564ac0de1b` (2026-10-31), moved onto the custom-speculator interface after #63205 replaced the config and factory integration this PR used; see the revision history below. This is the only Uno PR; the open interface PRs #64844 and #64306 extend the same interface and add no speculator.

The change includes:

- A native MRV2 speculator that shares the target model, attention layers and KV cache with the drafter and applies the
  adapter only to noise rows, through the LoRA manager's public adapter-mapping call.
- Fused draft-input preparation in one kernel; the prompt length and the request count are runtime values, so it compiles once.
- Native request state, Gumbel sampling, verification, async scheduling and draft CUDA graphs; K lookahead KV slots
  with correct ownership at full acceptance, block boundaries, preemption and prefix-cache reuse. Near a request's length
  or context limit, the scheduler's existing per-request spec-token cap and lookahead cap apply; Uno adds no scheduler code.
- Registration as the `uno` general plugin (`vllm.general_plugins`); method options go in `speculator_options`.
- Startup and request validation (fail-closed for KV transfer, KV-sharing fast prefill, which would wrap the shared target and draft layers incorrectly and hand verification wrong prompt logits, pipeline/data/context parallelism, EPLB and elastic expert parallelism, MLA, chunked-local, static-sink and reference sliding-window attention, other unsupported attention layouts, request-specific LoRA; tensor parallelism is supported and the draft uses the target's degree), a Qwen3-8B recipe ([the Uno docs page](https://github.com/brntech/vllm/blob/uno-core-upstream/docs/features/speculative_decoding/uno.md)), CPU regression tests and end-to-end model tests.

**Changes outside Uno's own files** (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/uno*.py`, its tests and docs), against `564ac0de1b`:

| File | Lines | What |
|---|---:|---|
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` | +2 | a generic `speculator.set_lora_manager(...)` call after the speculator loads, when LoRA is enabled |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py` | +7 | that hook, a no-op on `DraftModelSpeculator` |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator_config.py` | +1 | a `supports_request_lora` capability (default `True`; Uno sets `False`) |
| `vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py` | +8 | refuses a request-specific LoRA adapter when the speculator declares it unsupported |
| `pyproject.toml` | +1 | the `uno` general-plugin entry point |
| `.buildkite/test_areas/spec_decode.yaml` | +48 | the Uno jobs |
| `tests/v1/core/` | +282 / -1 | scheduler and prefix-caching cases for Uno's lookahead slots |

`vllm/config/`, the speculator factory, `scheduler.py`, `async_scheduler.py`, `sched/output.py` and `warmup.py` are unchanged.

**Platforms.** Uno runs on NVIDIA GPUs with the `FLASH_ATTN` or `TRITON_ATTN` attention backend, and on AMD ROCm GPUs with `--attention-config '{"backend":"TRITON_ATTN"}'`. It restricts the attention backend, not the card: it admits exactly the backends its tests run, and any other attention backend (FlashInfer included), or on ROCm an unset backend, is refused when the config is validated, before weights load. A backend must also pass the capability checks Uno already had (native draft decode metadata updates; graph support for draft graphs), and `load_model` re-checks the backend each layer built. On ROCm, Uno was tested on the Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201) at the previous head and is not re-run in this revision; this revision is re-verified on NVIDIA on one RTX 3090 (sm_86) with both backends.

Initial scope is NVIDIA GPUs (single GPU and tensor parallel) and AMD ROCm GPUs (tested single-GPU on the Radeon AI PRO R9700), text-only decoder models with one homogeneous full-attention KV group, the attention backends above, Model Runner V2 with async scheduling. A draft decode graph is captured only when some `cudagraph_capture_sizes` entry is at most `max_num_seqs * K`. Config-visible attention kinds are refused before weights load; model-specific layouts that no config key names (for example Inkling's local layers or per-layer sliding windows) are refused once the layers are built, with a clear message. The documented adapter is the original [`s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B`](https://huggingface.co/s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B) for `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`.

Uno is introduced in [Unlocking Lossless Speedups in LLMs via Discrete Diffusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04010); the method and adapter are credited to its authors. Development was assisted by AI tools. A ready-to-run container of the previous revision is published at [github.com/brntech/vllm-uno](https://github.com/brntech/vllm-uno) (release v0.2.0, image `ghcr.io/brntech/vllm-uno:0.2.0`).

## Test Plan

Base: `564ac0de1b` (main, 2026-10-31).

CPU (container, Python 3.12, no GPU):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_config.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_prepare_mrv2.py \
       tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_lora_mrv2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_mrv2.py \
       tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_preemption.py -q
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_custom_speculator.py tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_override.py -q
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
       tests/v1/engine/test_preprocess_error_handling.py -k uno -q
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only upstream/main HEAD)
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --all-files
```

GPU. This revision ran the Uno CI commands on an RTX 3090 (sm_86) with `FLASH_ATTN` and with `TRITON_ATTN`:

```bash
pytest -v -s v1/spec_decode/test_uno_config.py -k plugin_registers_in_a_fresh_process
pytest -v -s v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py -k "(greedy_matches_base_model and not max_model_len) or requires_effective_backend"
pytest -v -s v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py -k "max_model_len or survivor or prebuilt"
```

Earlier heads were tested on NVIDIA Ampere, Hopper and Blackwell, single GPU and tensor parallel. The recorded Python-source overlay reproduces every GPU run on the base's per-commit CI image. Earlier revisions were run on a GB10 (Blackwell sm_121, ARM64), an H100 PCIe and an H100 NVL (FlashAttention 2 and 3), and at tensor-parallel 2 on two RTX 5090s (Blackwell sm_120); the 10-11 head was run on an RTX 3090 (Ampere sm_86) and an AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, ROCm 7.2):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_prepare_mrv2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_lora_mrv2.py -x -v
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_gumbel_sample.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py \
  -k 'logits_cache or drafting_uses_a_separate_noise_stream or greedy_temperature_zero or gumbel_drafted_rejection_sample_is_unbiased or greedy_rejection_sample or chunked_requests_match_full_batch or placeholder_draft_token_rejected' \
  -v
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py -v -s
# The greedy matrix on TRITON_ATTN on NVIDIA:
VLLM_UNO_TEST_ATTENTION_BACKEND=TRITON_ATTN pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py::test_uno_greedy_matches_base_model -v -s
# On ROCm the e2e module runs on TRITON_ATTN by default:
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_*.py tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py -v -s
```

## Test Result

Throughput, latency, and the GB10, H100 and R9700 results below were measured at earlier heads; this revision was re-verified for lossless output on an RTX 3090, and throughput was not re-measured at this head.

### Throughput over plain vLLM

Every ratio is Uno divided by plain vLLM measured on the same card with the same client, model, precision and serving shape, in output tokens per second. GB10 and RTX 3090 figures are medians of three measured repeats after one warm-up; the H100 study reports mean per-prompt throughput at one stream and means of three warm batches at eight and 32 streams.

| Card | Workload | 1 stream | 4 / 8 streams | 16 / 32 streams |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| H100, earlier optimized MRV1 build (Qwen3-8B bf16, controlled, prefix caching off) | math | **2.58x** | 2.20x (8) | 1.74x (32) |
| GB10, this line at `49ffe316bb` (Qwen3-8B bf16, production shape) | short chat | **2.36x** | 1.31x (4) | 1.14x (16) |
| GB10 | long prompts | **2.21x** | 1.44x (4) | 1.15x (16) |
| GB10 | mixed | **2.06x** | 1.58x (4) | 1.12x (16) |
| RTX 3090, head `5da19391` (Qwen3-8B bf16, production shape) | short chat | **1.65x** | 1.18x (4) | 0.74x (16) |
| RTX 3090 | long prompts | **1.71x** | 1.13x (4) | 0.77x (16) |
| RTX 3090 | mixed | **1.85x** | 1.46x (4) | 0.72x (16) |

The H100 row is our earlier optimized Model Runner V1 implementation of the same design, measured in
[the study that IFM cites](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22652610) (single-prompt operating points on the same card: math 375 tokens/s, code 306, prose 212). The GB10 rows are this MRV2 line at `49ffe316bb` and the RTX 3090 rows head `5da19391`, both under one identical production shape (K=8, async scheduling, ctx 4096, `max_num_seqs` 16, 2048 batched tokens, 2 GiB KV, prefix caching, 128 output tokens). On the same GB10, with the optimized MRV1 release measured as a third arm, MRV2 exceeded it in all nine cells, by 1.03 to 1.31x. Uno is ahead wherever the card has compute headroom to verify drafts in: at four streams on every card, at sixteen on the GB10, at 32 on the H100. The reference SGLang implementation, measured on the same H100 against the same plain server, lands at 2.60x / 2.24x / 1.79x, within 3% of the H100 build at every concurrency.

### First-token latency

At head `5da19391`, same card, same client, median of three repeats: single-stream steady first token Uno 28.0 / 28.2 / 30.5 ms against plain 26.8 / 26.8 / 29.1 ms (short / mixed / long). The draft-input kernel takes the prompt length and the request count as runtime values, so it never recompiles for a new length or batch size. Since the rework there is no startup warmup of the draft sampler, so the first request compiles its sampler kernels.

### Lossless output

**Greedy exact-token matrix.** Seven K=1/K=8 cases (eager, CUDA graphs, prefix caching, dual-stream LoRA) compare Uno's greedy tokens with the plain engine's, each with a same-arm plain-vs-plain control. A first divergence is excused only where the plain engine's own top two raw logits are one bfloat16 step apart at that position, at most one prompt per batch, and every excused position is printed. Each case prints an instrument line (card, compute capability, graph mode, attention version, control coordinates, tie positions). Since the 10-11 head the matrix also asserts that the attention implementation built is the requested backend's. At the 10-11 head: RTX 3090, `TRITON_ATTN`: 7/7, every batch exact in tokens and text, no tie excused. RTX 3090, `FLASH_ATTN`: 7/7, exact except one excused tie in each of two cases (raw-logit gaps 0 and one bfloat16 step, at positions earlier rounds also met). R9700, `TRITON_ATTN`: 7/7, exact, no tie excused. Earlier heads: 7/7 on the GB10 and on the H100 under both FlashAttention 3 and 2.

**Context limit.** A nightly test serves four concurrent requests to `max_model_len` at K=8 and audits every draft KV slot against the limit and the request's block-table row; all four finish at exactly `max_model_len` with tokens and text equal to the plain engine's, and no draft row writes a slot at or past the limit.

**Sampled output.** Sampled-distribution permutation tests (256 samples for each of three prefixes, 16 tokens) pass for both Uno arms and for the independent plain-repeat control; raw greedy matches are 7/8 for both Uno arms against plain and 7/8 for plain against itself on a same-server repeat. GSM8K-128 (five-shot, temperature zero): plain 119/128, Uno MRV2 118/128, optimized MRV1 117/128.

### Request features under speculative decoding

Structured output (valid JSON from a `json_schema` request), logprobs, repetition and presence penalties and `ignore_eos` are all served with Uno drafting active. Min-p and logit bias are refused at admission by vLLM's general spec-decode guard, the same one EAGLE-3 hits. A request-specific LoRA adapter is refused before it is queued; a request can never select Uno's own adapter, including through a prebuilt `EngineCoreRequest` (a nightly test checks both, with exact outputs and the engine serving on).

### Continuous batching under KV pressure

The survivor test pins a 69-block KV pool, admits a seed request, two long peers and an abort peer, and asserts that a long peer is preempted while still generating and that its tokens after resumption equal its solo run. The pool is sized to force the crossing even when one long peer stalls at its admission footprint. It passed on the GB10, the H100 NVL (FlashAttention 3 and 2) at the 10-11 head on the RTX 3090 and the R9700, and at this head on the RTX 3090 with both backends. The test records the preemption at the scheduler's own event, resolves requests by the scheduler's internal ids, and writes its diagnostics to a file, so a non-firing run fails with a trace instead of skipping.

### Test counts

At the current head (`564ac0de1b` base): CPU Uno modules 210 passed, 14 skipped; the custom-speculator interface tests 65 passed, the same IDs and outcomes as on main; pre-commit clean. On an RTX 3090 (sm_86), for both `FLASH_ATTN` and `TRITON_ATTN`: the regular Uno job 13/13 (the 7-case greedy matrix and the six pre-weight admission cases, which fail on main because the feature is absent there), the nightly group 3/3, and 8/8 HTTP requests served per backend. Expert load balancing being refused before weights load has CPU coverage only; it needs two GPUs.

At the 10-11 head: CPU Uno modules 187 passed; pre-commit and mypy 3.12 clean (model runner V2 and factory 37, scheduler and prefix caching 391 at the previous head; this revision changes none of their files). The GPU rows below ran one local revision earlier; the only code change since removes an AMD chip check, so the unit suite now has one admission case fewer.

| Platform | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `FLASH_ATTN` | Uno unit tests | 202 passed |
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `FLASH_ATTN` | nightly group: context limit + KV-slot audit, survivor, prebuilt LoRA | 3/3 |
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `FLASH_ATTN` | 7-case greedy matrix | 7/7 (two excused bf16 ties) |
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `TRITON_ATTN` | 7-case greedy matrix | 7/7, no excused ties |
| Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), `TRITON_ATTN` | Uno unit tests | 202 passed |
| Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), `TRITON_ATTN` | e2e module: matrix, context limit, survivor, prebuilt LoRA | 10/10, no excused ties |

No package dependencies are added. The Uno Buildkite jobs trigger on the spec-decode paths, the core files this PR edits and the LoRA and scheduler paths Uno wraps. The regular job runs plugin registration, the greedy matrix and the pre-weight admission cases; the context-limit, survivor and prebuilt-request tests run in a nightly job.

## Not in this patch

Three optimisations are left out to keep changes to vLLM's core files minimal. Each would first need a small generic hook, and can follow as a separate PR if wanted:

- **Early length-tail policy:** stop drafting on a step that may be a request's last, saving `K` lookahead KV rows near its length or context limit. Needs a per-request "next draft width" that a speculator can set.
- **Startup draft warmup:** compile the draft sampler's kernels at startup instead of on the first request. Needs a speculator warmup hook beside the existing dummy-propose warmup.
- **Cached LoRA metadata:** reuse precomputed adapter mappings for the draft rows instead of rebuilding them every step. Needs a public way to reuse a LoRA mapping.

Together they are worth about 2% at 16 concurrent requests on an RTX 3090 (Qwen3-8B, K=8, 16 greedy chats × 256 tokens, 3 repeats: 710.7 vs 726.2 tokens/s); single-stream is unchanged within noise (103.6 vs 104.4).

## Revision history

**2026-11-01, custom-speculator interface.** Rebased onto main `564ac0de1b` after #63205 replaced the config and factory integration this PR used. Uno now registers through that interface as the `uno` general plugin, so `vllm/config/` and the speculator factory are untouched; method options moved into `speculator_options`. The request-LoRA refusal is a `supports_request_lora` capability on `SpeculatorConfig` instead of a method check. Admission before weights load now also refuses EPLB and elastic expert parallelism, MLA, chunked-local, static-sink and reference sliding-window attention, and requires an explicit full-attention backend. The Uno CI jobs also trigger on the core files this PR edits. Re-verified on an RTX 3090 with `FLASH_ATTN` and `TRITON_ATTN`; ROCm was not re-run in this revision.

**2026-10-11, AMD ROCm.** Uno runs on AMD ROCm GPUs with `TRITON_ATTN` (tested on the Radeon AI PRO R9700, gfx1201), and on NVIDIA with `TRITON_ATTN` as well as `FLASH_ATTN`. It admits exactly the attention backends its tests run: any other backend, FlashInfer included, and an unset backend on ROCm, are refused when the config is validated, before weights load. Only Uno's own files change; the core footprint is unchanged. The greedy matrix asserts the attention implementation it built, and the survivor test no longer holds its in-process engine across the runner exit (only ROCm's teardown memory wait caught that reference).

**2026-10-11, rework.** Uno now stays out of vLLM's core files. `scheduler.py`, `async_scheduler.py`, `sched/output.py` and `warmup.py` are back to main; the V2 model runner change is a two-line call to a generic `set_lora_manager` speculator hook (a no-op on `BaseSpeculator`), and Uno's serving checks moved next to the method. Dropped: the early length-tail policy (the scheduler's existing per-request cap and lookahead cap keep the context limit correct, checked by a new nightly test that audits every draft KV slot), the startup draft warmup (the draft-input kernel takes the request count as a runtime value instead), and the cached LoRA-metadata restore (draft rows use the LoRA manager's public mapping call). A request-specific LoRA adapter is refused in the input processor, and no request can select Uno's own adapter. The greedy matrix counts ties in bfloat16 steps of the raw logits. The Uno CI job triggers on spec-decode paths only; the longer end-to-end tests run nightly.

**2026-10-10, merge of main `ff440c7805`.** Conflict resolved in the V2 model runner: #60754 moved the drafter hidden-state helper to `spec_decode.utils.get_drafter_hidden_states` and renamed `dp_sync` to `dp_sync_state`; Uno's proposal path and `propose()` follow both. API adaptations: #60736 (request-slot index mappings are int64; Uno's draft sample mapping follows, and the fused input preparation refuses a non-int64 one) and #57169 (packed KV layout: `BlockTables.kernel_block_sizes` is gone, so Uno's slot preparation reads `block_sizes`, without which the engine failed at warmup; the draft graph replay maps the kernel block table first). Method and scope are unchanged.

**2026-10-06, merge of main `385d86a6cf`.** Conflicts resolved in the V2 model runner (#40704) and in the imports of `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`. Method and scope are unchanged.

**2026-10-05, merge of main `74c5cbcd7b`.** Conflicts resolved in `vllm/config/vllm.py` (Uno's lookahead rule beside #59105's fill-in DSpark rule) and the V2 model runner (#57053, dynamic K: Uno requires a fixed `num_speculative_tokens` and `UnoSpeculator.propose` accepts the new argument). Method and scope are unchanged.

**2026-10-04, merge of main `84bcbc6264`.** Conflicts resolved in `spec_decode.yaml` (#57237's split), `tests/v1/core/utils.py`, `vllm/config/vllm.py` (`dflash` and `uno` on the async allowlists), the scheduler and the V2 model runner; adapted to #56497, #56807 and test-side changes from #55939, #58459, #58784 and #59359.

**2026-09-17, cleanup pass (on a fresh merge of main `91a4c40b45`).** The per-step timing tracer, the launch-key debug module and the JIT-monitor hooks were removed entirely, with their switches and scheduler-output fields.

**2026-09-16.** Merged with main at `af1c0149`; a pre-commit fix; DCO sign-off on the two commits.

**2026-09-14.** Model Runner V2 revision replaces the V1 revision; rebased onto main at `b87339888d`.

Updated this PR to the Model Runner V2 implementation discussed in #55267, rebased onto main at `b87339888d`. Full tables and
receipts are in the description; a ready-to-run container of this revision is at
[github.com/brntech/vllm-uno](https://github.com/brntech/vllm-uno) (v0.2.0, `ghcr.io/brntech/vllm-uno:0.2.0`).

**What changed since the MRV1 revision.** The MRV1 code is replaced rather than kept alongside; the previous MRV1 head (`71184d4`) is
not an ancestor of the new head and is preserved on `uno-core-upstream-mrv1` and in our released package (v0.1.0 of the same repository).
Scope of the new head: native MRV2 speculator (shared target weights and KV, adapter only on noise rows, native Gumbel
sampling/verification/async scheduling/draft graphs, fused draft preparation, bounded Punica-metadata cache), fail-closed validation,
a Qwen3-8B recipe, CPU tests and end-to-end model tests. Since the last measured build: fail-closed refusal of KV-sharing fast prefill,
tensor parallelism allowed (pipeline, data and context parallelism remain refused), a startup line reporting draft CUDA-graph coverage
per request count, startup warm-up of every served draft launch with a JIT-monitor self-check, and the end of drafting for a request
near its length or context limit. On the same GB10, this line (`49ffe316bb`) exceeded the optimized MRV1 release in all nine measured
cells, by 1.03 to 1.31x.

**Tested on Ampere, Hopper and Blackwell, single GPU and tensor parallel.** This revision was run end-to-end on an RTX 3090, a GB10 and
an H100 NVL (module 8/8, survivor and matrix pass on all three; on the H100 under both FlashAttention 3 and FlashAttention 2, each
named by the engine log and the test receipt), and at tensor-parallel 2 on two RTX 5090s (Uno's greedy tokens equal the plain engine's
at each TP degree). The continuous-batching survivor test forces a real preemption under a pinned KV pool and checks the resumed
request's tokens against its solo run; the resumed peer matched its solo tokens on the GB10 (preempted at 262 generated tokens), on
the RTX 3090 (three preemptions) and on the H100 (261 under FlashAttention 3, 262 under FlashAttention 2).

**Lossless.** The greedy exact-token matrix passes 7/7 on the GB10, on the H100 under both FlashAttention versions and on the 3090 under
the separate-engine control; on the GB10 and H100 the plain-vs-plain control is exact in every case, and on the 3090 in graph mode,
where the plain engine does not reproduce itself bit-exactly across processes, the tie-aware control shows Uno diverging nowhere the
plain engine does not. Sampled-distribution permutation tests pass for both Uno arms and the plain-repeat control; GSM8K-128 is

of the earlier gap are gone: the draft-input kernel specialised on prompt length and recompiled per length, and a draft proposal that
ran after a request's final token.

The implementation is organized so it can be reviewed, or split, as four parts: configuration and validation, the MRV2 speculator,
fused preparation and the Punica cache, and documentation and tests.

raw_graphql_pull_request.title: [Feature][Spec Decode] Add Uno shared-model drafting with a draft-only LoRA adapter (Model Runner V2)

repo.description: A high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs
repo.name: vllm

detail.body:
**TL;DR.** Speculative decoding with no separate draft model: the target model drafts its own candidates through a small LoRA adapter, and vLLM's native rejection sampler verifies them. Measured against plain vLLM on the same card, same client and same serving shape: **2.1 to 2.4x single-stream on a GB10 and 1.7 to 1.9x on an RTX 3090** with this implementation, and **2.6x on an H100** with our earlier Model Runner V1 build of the same design, which this implementation beats in every cell measured side by side. It stays ahead under load (1.1 to 1.6x at four and sixteen streams on the GB10; 2.2x at eight streams and 1.7x at 32 on the H100). Output is lossless: greedy tokens match plain wherever plain reproduces itself, sampled-distribution tests pass, GSM8K is within one answer of plain. Uno now plugs in through the custom-speculator interface from #63205, registered as a general plugin: outside its own modules the PR adds 19 lines in five core files and no configuration code. Earlier heads were tested on NVIDIA Ampere, Hopper (FlashAttention 2 and 3) and Blackwell, single GPU and tensor parallel, and on an AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (ROCm, TRITON_ATTN); this revision is re-verified on an RTX 3090 with `FLASH_ATTN` and `TRITON_ATTN`. The reference SGLang implementation lands within 3% of the H100 build at every concurrency.

## Purpose

Adds native Uno self-drafting through `speculative_config.method="uno"` for Model Runner V2. One target model
produces `K` draft candidates per request from one base-weight seed row and `K-1` noise rows routed through the Uno
adapter; verification uses the native MRV2 rejection sampler. This follows the MRV2 direction agreed in
[RFC #55267](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55267). The earlier revision of this PR targeted Model Runner V1; this revision replaces it. Current head: on main at `564ac0de1b` (2026-10-31), moved onto the custom-speculator interface after #63205 replaced the config and factory integration this PR used; see the revision history below. This is the only Uno PR; the open interface PRs #64844 and #64306 extend the same interface and add no speculator.

The change includes:

- A native MRV2 speculator that shares the target model, attention layers and KV cache with the drafter and applies the
  adapter only to noise rows, through the LoRA manager's public adapter-mapping call.
- Fused draft-input preparation in one kernel; the prompt length and the request count are runtime values, so it compiles once.
- Native request state, Gumbel sampling, verification, async scheduling and draft CUDA graphs; K lookahead KV slots
  with correct ownership at full acceptance, block boundaries, preemption and prefix-cache reuse. Near a request's length
  or context limit, the scheduler's existing per-request spec-token cap and lookahead cap apply; Uno adds no scheduler code.
- Registration as the `uno` general plugin (`vllm.general_plugins`); method options go in `speculator_options`.
- Startup and request validation (fail-closed for KV transfer, KV-sharing fast prefill, which would wrap the shared target and draft layers incorrectly and hand verification wrong prompt logits, pipeline/data/context parallelism, EPLB and elastic expert parallelism, MLA, chunked-local, static-sink and reference sliding-window attention, other unsupported attention layouts, request-specific LoRA; tensor parallelism is supported and the draft uses the target's degree), a Qwen3-8B recipe ([the Uno docs page](https://github.com/brntech/vllm/blob/uno-core-upstream/docs/features/speculative_decoding/uno.md)), CPU regression tests and end-to-end model tests.

**Changes outside Uno's own files** (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/uno*.py`, its tests and docs), against `564ac0de1b`:

| File | Lines | What |
|---|---:|---|
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` | +2 | a generic `speculator.set_lora_manager(...)` call after the speculator loads, when LoRA is enabled |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py` | +7 | that hook, a no-op on `DraftModelSpeculator` |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator_config.py` | +1 | a `supports_request_lora` capability (default `True`; Uno sets `False`) |
| `vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py` | +8 | refuses a request-specific LoRA adapter when the speculator declares it unsupported |
| `pyproject.toml` | +1 | the `uno` general-plugin entry point |
| `.buildkite/test_areas/spec_decode.yaml` | +48 | the Uno jobs |
| `tests/v1/core/` | +282 / -1 | scheduler and prefix-caching cases for Uno's lookahead slots |

`vllm/config/`, the speculator factory, `scheduler.py`, `async_scheduler.py`, `sched/output.py` and `warmup.py` are unchanged.

**Platforms.** Uno runs on NVIDIA GPUs with the `FLASH_ATTN` or `TRITON_ATTN` attention backend, and on AMD ROCm GPUs with `--attention-config '{"backend":"TRITON_ATTN"}'`. It restricts the attention backend, not the card: it admits exactly the backends its tests run, and any other attention backend (FlashInfer included), or on ROCm an unset backend, is refused when the config is validated, before weights load. A backend must also pass the capability checks Uno already had (native draft decode metadata updates; graph support for draft graphs), and `load_model` re-checks the backend each layer built. On ROCm, Uno was tested on the Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201) at the previous head and is not re-run in this revision; this revision is re-verified on NVIDIA on one RTX 3090 (sm_86) with both backends.

Initial scope is NVIDIA GPUs (single GPU and tensor parallel) and AMD ROCm GPUs (tested single-GPU on the Radeon AI PRO R9700), text-only decoder models with one homogeneous full-attention KV group, the attention backends above, Model Runner V2 with async scheduling. A draft decode graph is captured only when some `cudagraph_capture_sizes` entry is at most `max_num_seqs * K`. Config-visible attention kinds are refused before weights load; model-specific layouts that no config key names (for example Inkling's local layers or per-layer sliding windows) are refused once the layers are built, with a clear message. The documented adapter is the original [`s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B`](https://huggingface.co/s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B) for `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`.

Uno is introduced in [Unlocking Lossless Speedups in LLMs via Discrete Diffusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04010); the method and adapter are credited to its authors. Development was assisted by AI tools. A ready-to-run container of the previous revision is published at [github.com/brntech/vllm-uno](https://github.com/brntech/vllm-uno) (release v0.2.0, image `ghcr.io/brntech/vllm-uno:0.2.0`).

## Test Plan

Base: `564ac0de1b` (main, 2026-10-31).

CPU (container, Python 3.12, no GPU):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_config.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_prepare_mrv2.py \
       tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_lora_mrv2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_mrv2.py \
       tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_preemption.py -q
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_custom_speculator.py tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_override.py -q
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
       tests/v1/engine/test_preprocess_error_handling.py -k uno -q
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only upstream/main HEAD)
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --all-files
```

GPU. This revision ran the Uno CI commands on an RTX 3090 (sm_86) with `FLASH_ATTN` and with `TRITON_ATTN`:

```bash
pytest -v -s v1/spec_decode/test_uno_config.py -k plugin_registers_in_a_fresh_process
pytest -v -s v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py -k "(greedy_matches_base_model and not max_model_len) or requires_effective_backend"
pytest -v -s v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py -k "max_model_len or survivor or prebuilt"
```

Earlier heads were tested on NVIDIA Ampere, Hopper and Blackwell, single GPU and tensor parallel. The recorded Python-source overlay reproduces every GPU run on the base's per-commit CI image. Earlier revisions were run on a GB10 (Blackwell sm_121, ARM64), an H100 PCIe and an H100 NVL (FlashAttention 2 and 3), and at tensor-parallel 2 on two RTX 5090s (Blackwell sm_120); the 10-11 head was run on an RTX 3090 (Ampere sm_86) and an AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, ROCm 7.2):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_prepare_mrv2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_lora_mrv2.py -x -v
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_gumbel_sample.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py \
  -k 'logits_cache or drafting_uses_a_separate_noise_stream or greedy_temperature_zero or gumbel_drafted_rejection_sample_is_unbiased or greedy_rejection_sample or chunked_requests_match_full_batch or placeholder_draft_token_rejected' \
  -v
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py -v -s
# The greedy matrix on TRITON_ATTN on NVIDIA:
VLLM_UNO_TEST_ATTENTION_BACKEND=TRITON_ATTN pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py::test_uno_greedy_matches_base_model -v -s
# On ROCm the e2e module runs on TRITON_ATTN by default:
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_uno_*.py tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_uno.py -v -s
```

## Test Result

Throughput, latency, and the GB10, H100 and R9700 results below were measured at earlier heads; this revision was re-verified for lossless output on an RTX 3090, and throughput was not re-measured at this head.

### Throughput over plain vLLM

Every ratio is Uno divided by plain vLLM measured on the same card with the same client, model, precision and serving shape, in output tokens per second. GB10 and RTX 3090 figures are medians of three measured repeats after one warm-up; the H100 study reports mean per-prompt throughput at one stream and means of three warm batches at eight and 32 streams.

| Card | Workload | 1 stream | 4 / 8 streams | 16 / 32 streams |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| H100, earlier optimized MRV1 build (Qwen3-8B bf16, controlled, prefix caching off) | math | **2.58x** | 2.20x (8) | 1.74x (32) |
| GB10, this line at `49ffe316bb` (Qwen3-8B bf16, production shape) | short chat | **2.36x** | 1.31x (4) | 1.14x (16) |
| GB10 | long prompts | **2.21x** | 1.44x (4) | 1.15x (16) |
| GB10 | mixed | **2.06x** | 1.58x (4) | 1.12x (16) |
| RTX 3090, head `5da19391` (Qwen3-8B bf16, production shape) | short chat | **1.65x** | 1.18x (4) | 0.74x (16) |
| RTX 3090 | long prompts | **1.71x** | 1.13x (4) | 0.77x (16) |
| RTX 3090 | mixed | **1.85x** | 1.46x (4) | 0.72x (16) |

The H100 row is our earlier optimized Model Runner V1 implementation of the same design, measured in
[the study that IFM cites](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22652610) (single-prompt operating points on the same card: math 375 tokens/s, code 306, prose 212). The GB10 rows are this MRV2 line at `49ffe316bb` and the RTX 3090 rows head `5da19391`, both under one identical production shape (K=8, async scheduling, ctx 4096, `max_num_seqs` 16, 2048 batched tokens, 2 GiB KV, prefix caching, 128 output tokens). On the same GB10, with the optimized MRV1 release measured as a third arm, MRV2 exceeded it in all nine cells, by 1.03 to 1.31x. Uno is ahead wherever the card has compute headroom to verify drafts in: at four streams on every card, at sixteen on the GB10, at 32 on the H100. The reference SGLang implementation, measured on the same H100 against the same plain server, lands at 2.60x / 2.24x / 1.79x, within 3% of the H100 build at every concurrency.

### First-token latency

At head `5da19391`, same card, same client, median of three repeats: single-stream steady first token Uno 28.0 / 28.2 / 30.5 ms against plain 26.8 / 26.8 / 29.1 ms (short / mixed / long). The draft-input kernel takes the prompt length and the request count as runtime values, so it never recompiles for a new length or batch size. Since the rework there is no startup warmup of the draft sampler, so the first request compiles its sampler kernels.

### Lossless output

**Greedy exact-token matrix.** Seven K=1/K=8 cases (eager, CUDA graphs, prefix caching, dual-stream LoRA) compare Uno's greedy tokens with the plain engine's, each with a same-arm plain-vs-plain control. A first divergence is excused only where the plain engine's own top two raw logits are one bfloat16 step apart at that position, at most one prompt per batch, and every excused position is printed. Each case prints an instrument line (card, compute capability, graph mode, attention version, control coordinates, tie positions). Since the 10-11 head the matrix also asserts that the attention implementation built is the requested backend's. At the 10-11 head: RTX 3090, `TRITON_ATTN`: 7/7, every batch exact in tokens and text, no tie excused. RTX 3090, `FLASH_ATTN`: 7/7, exact except one excused tie in each of two cases (raw-logit gaps 0 and one bfloat16 step, at positions earlier rounds also met). R9700, `TRITON_ATTN`: 7/7, exact, no tie excused. Earlier heads: 7/7 on the GB10 and on the H100 under both FlashAttention 3 and 2.

**Context limit.** A nightly test serves four concurrent requests to `max_model_len` at K=8 and audits every draft KV slot against the limit and the request's block-table row; all four finish at exactly `max_model_len` with tokens and text equal to the plain engine's, and no draft row writes a slot at or past the limit.

**Sampled output.** Sampled-distribution permutation tests (256 samples for each of three prefixes, 16 tokens) pass for both Uno arms and for the independent plain-repeat control; raw greedy matches are 7/8 for both Uno arms against plain and 7/8 for plain against itself on a same-server repeat. GSM8K-128 (five-shot, temperature zero): plain 119/128, Uno MRV2 118/128, optimized MRV1 117/128.

### Request features under speculative decoding

Structured output (valid JSON from a `json_schema` request), logprobs, repetition and presence penalties and `ignore_eos` are all served with Uno drafting active. Min-p and logit bias are refused at admission by vLLM's general spec-decode guard, the same one EAGLE-3 hits. A request-specific LoRA adapter is refused before it is queued; a request can never select Uno's own adapter, including through a prebuilt `EngineCoreRequest` (a nightly test checks both, with exact outputs and the engine serving on).

### Continuous batching under KV pressure

The survivor test pins a 69-block KV pool, admits a seed request, two long peers and an abort peer, and asserts that a long peer is preempted while still generating and that its tokens after resumption equal its solo run. The pool is sized to force the crossing even when one long peer stalls at its admission footprint. It passed on the GB10, the H100 NVL (FlashAttention 3 and 2) at the 10-11 head on the RTX 3090 and the R9700, and at this head on the RTX 3090 with both backends. The test records the preemption at the scheduler's own event, resolves requests by the scheduler's internal ids, and writes its diagnostics to a file, so a non-firing run fails with a trace instead of skipping.

### Test counts

At the current head (`564ac0de1b` base): CPU Uno modules 210 passed, 14 skipped; the custom-speculator interface tests 65 passed, the same IDs and outcomes as on main; pre-commit clean. On an RTX 3090 (sm_86), for both `FLASH_ATTN` and `TRITON_ATTN`: the regular Uno job 13/13 (the 7-case greedy matrix and the six pre-weight admission cases, which fail on main because the feature is absent there), the nightly group 3/3, and 8/8 HTTP requests served per backend. Expert load balancing being refused before weights load has CPU coverage only; it needs two GPUs.

At the 10-11 head: CPU Uno modules 187 passed; pre-commit and mypy 3.12 clean (model runner V2 and factory 37, scheduler and prefix caching 391 at the previous head; this revision changes none of their files). The GPU rows below ran one local revision earlier; the only code change since removes an AMD chip check, so the unit suite now has one admission case fewer.

| Platform | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `FLASH_ATTN` | Uno unit tests | 202 passed |
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `FLASH_ATTN` | nightly group: context limit + KV-slot audit, survivor, prebuilt LoRA | 3/3 |
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `FLASH_ATTN` | 7-case greedy matrix | 7/7 (two excused bf16 ties) |
| RTX 3090 (sm_86), `TRITON_ATTN` | 7-case greedy matrix | 7/7, no excused ties |
| Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), `TRITON_ATTN` | Uno unit tests | 202 passed |
| Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201), `TRITON_ATTN` | e2e module: matrix, context limit, survivor, prebuilt LoRA | 10/10, no excused ties |

No package dependencies are added. The Uno Buildkite jobs trigger on the spec-decode paths, the core files this PR edits and the LoRA and scheduler paths Uno wraps. The regular job runs plugin registration, the greedy matrix and the pre-weight admission cases; the context-limit, survivor and prebuilt-request tests run in a nightly job.

## Not in this patch

Three optimisations are left out to keep changes to vLLM's core files minimal. Each would first need a small generic hook, and can follow as a separate PR if wanted:

- **Early length-tail policy:** stop drafting on a step that may be a request's last, saving `K` lookahead KV rows near its length or context limit. Needs a per-request "next draft width" that a speculator can set.
- **Startup draft warmup:** compile the draft sampler's kernels at startup instead of on the first request. Needs a speculator warmup hook beside the existing dummy-propose warmup.
- **Cached LoRA metadata:** reuse precomputed adapter mappings for the draft rows instead of rebuilding them every step. Needs a public way to reuse a LoRA mapping.

Together they are worth about 2% at 16 concurrent requests on an RTX 3090 (Qwen3-8B, K=8, 16 greedy chats × 256 tokens, 3 repeats: 710.7 vs 726.2 tokens/s); single-stream is unchanged within noise (103.6 vs 104.4).

## Revision history

**2026-11-01, custom-speculator interface.** Rebased onto main `564ac0de1b` after #63205 replaced the config and factory integration this PR used. Uno now registers through that interface as the `uno` general plugin, so `vllm/config/` and the speculator factory are untouched; method options moved into `speculator_options`. The request-LoRA refusal is a `supports_request_lora` capability on `SpeculatorConfig` instead of a method check. Admission before weights load now also refuses EPLB and elastic expert parallelism, MLA, chunked-local, static-sink and reference sliding-window attention, and requires an explicit full-attention backend. The Uno CI jobs also trigger on the core files this PR edits. Re-verified on an RTX 3090 with `FLASH_ATTN` and `TRITON_ATTN`; ROCm was not re-run in this revision.

**2026-10-11, AMD ROCm.** Uno runs on AMD ROCm GPUs with `TRITON_ATTN` (tested on the Radeon AI PRO R9700, gfx1201), and on NVIDIA with `TRITON_ATTN` as well as `FLASH_ATTN`. It admits exactly the attention backends its tests run: any other backend, FlashInfer included, and an unset backend on ROCm, are refused when the config is validated, before weights load. Only Uno's own files change; the core footprint is unchanged. The greedy matrix asserts the attention implementation it built, and the survivor test no longer holds its in-process engine across the runner exit (only ROCm's teardown memory wait caught that reference).

**2026-10-11, rework.** Uno now stays out of vLLM's core files. `scheduler.py`, `async_scheduler.py`, `sched/output.py` and `warmup.py` are back to main; the V2 model runner change is a two-line call to a generic `set_lora_manager` speculator hook (a no-op on `BaseSpeculator`), and Uno's serving checks moved next to the method. Dropped: the early length-tail policy (the scheduler's existing per-request cap and lookahead cap keep the context limit correct, checked by a new nightly test that audits every draft KV slot), the startup draft warmup (the draft-input kernel takes the request count as a runtime value instead), and the cached LoRA-metadata restore (draft rows use the LoRA manager's public mapping call). A request-specific LoRA adapter is refused in the input processor, and no request can select Uno's own adapter. The greedy matrix counts ties in bfloat16 steps of the raw logits. The Uno CI job triggers on spec-decode paths only; the longer end-to-end tests run nightly.

**2026-10-10, merge of main `ff440c7805`.** Conflict resolved in the V2 model runner: #60754 moved the drafter hidden-state helper to `spec_decode.utils.get_drafter_hidden_states` and renamed `dp_sync` to `dp_sync_state`; Uno's proposal path and `propose()` follow both. API adaptations: #60736 (request-slot index mappings are int64; Uno's draft sample mapping follows, and the fused input preparation refuses a non-int64 one) and #57169 (packed KV layout: `BlockTables.kernel_block_sizes` is gone, so Uno's slot preparation reads `block_sizes`, without which the engine failed at warmup; the draft graph replay maps the kernel block table first). Method and scope are unchanged.

**2026-10-06, merge of main `385d86a6cf`.** Conflicts resolved in the V2 model runner (#40704) and in the imports of `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`. Method and scope are unchanged.

**2026-10-05, merge of main `74c5cbcd7b`.** Conflicts resolved in `vllm/config/vllm.py` (Uno's lookahead rule beside #59105's fill-in DSpark rule) and the V2 model runner (#57053, dynamic K: Uno requires a fixed `num_speculative_tokens` and `UnoSpeculator.propose` accepts the new argument). Method and scope are unchanged.

**2026-10-04, merge of main `84bcbc6264`.** Conflicts resolved in `spec_decode.yaml` (#57237's split), `tests/v1/core/utils.py`, `vllm/config/vllm.py` (`dflash` and `uno` on the async allowlists), the scheduler and the V2 model runner; adapted to #56497, #56807 and test-side changes from #55939, #58459, #58784 and #59359.

**2026-09-17, cleanup pass (on a fresh merge of main `91a4c40b45`).** The per-step timing tracer, the launch-key debug module and the JIT-monitor hooks were removed entirely, with their switches and scheduler-output fields.

**2026-09-16.** Merged with main at `af1c0149`; a pre-commit fix; DCO sign-off on the two commits.

**2026-09-14.** Model Runner V2 revision replaces the V1 revision; rebased onto main at `b87339888d`.

@@ -0,0 +1,68 @@
+# Uno
+
+[Uno](https://github.com/ifm-ai/uno) generates speculative candidates with the target model and a trained diffusion LoRA adapter. Model Runner V2 shares the target weights and KV cache with the drafter; no second base model is loaded.
+
+Each draft pass has one base-model seed row followed by `K-1` noisy rows routed through the Uno adapter. Those `K` rows propose `K` candidates in parallel. Draft attention exposes the committed prefix and earlier rows within the new block, as in the [original Uno implementation](https://github.com/ifm-ai/uno/blob/main/nano_vllm_uno/layers/attention.py). Target verification uses base weights and vLLM's native rejection sampler. Draft KV is temporary: rejected candidates and noise rows do not become verified prefix-cache entries.
+
+## Qwen3-8B example
+
+Start with `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` in BF16 and the original `s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B` adapter. Download the adapter's `adapter` subdirectory before starting the server:
+
+```python
+from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
+
+snapshot = snapshot_download(
+    "s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B",
+    revision="8819e09ac901e7290d8d89d62c98b9f756c602fe",
+    allow_patterns=["adapter/*"],
+)
+print(f"{snapshot}/adapter")
+```
+
+Use that directory as `/path/to/adapter` below:
+
+```bash
+VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
+    --revision b968826d9c46dd6066d109eabc6255188de91218 \
+    --dtype bfloat16 \
+    --enable-lora --max-lora-rank 128 --max-loras 2 \
+    --async-scheduling \
+    --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASH_ATTN","flash_attn_version":2}' \
+    --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
+    --speculative-config '{"method":"uno","num_speculative_tokens":8,"speculator_options":{"uno_lora_path":"/path/to/adapter","uno_mask_token_id":151669}}'
+```
+
+Normal sampling settings, including greedy decoding, temperature, top-k and top-p, apply to the target distribution. For the Qwen3 non-thinking profile, pass `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` in chat requests.
+
+## Configuration and scope
+
+Uno is registered by the `uno` general plugin. If `VLLM_PLUGINS` is set, include `uno` in its allowlist. Method-specific options go inside `speculator_options`; unknown options are rejected.
+
+Set the effective full-attention backend explicitly on both CUDA and ROCm, using
+`attention_config.backend` or `backend_per_kind.full_attention`. An override for
+another KV kind does not select Uno's backend. Layer-specific selector inputs
+can differ from a config-only prediction, so Uno requires this explicit choice
+before loading weights and checks the actual layer backends after construction.
+
+- `uno_lora_path` is required and points to a PEFT adapter. Use an adapter trained for the exact base model.
+- `num_speculative_tokens` is a fixed positive `K`. `K=1` exercises the seed-only path. The registered speculator drafts all rows in parallel.
+- `uno_mask_token_id` is the exclusive upper bound of the uniform noise range `[1, uno_mask_token_id)`, not a fixed token inserted into every noisy row. Match the training configuration; the default is the target vocabulary size.
+- `uno_noise_seed` controls deterministic input noise for a fixed request seed, batch row order and draft step. The released hash includes the flat batch-row term, so noise is not invariant to batch reordering. Request sampling seeds retain their normal meaning.
+- `max_loras` must be at least `2`; Uno reserves one slot for its shared adapter while native graph setup may use another slot.
+- `max_num_batched_tokens` must be at least `max_num_seqs * K` to fit the draft queries and native LoRA metadata buffers.
+
+The initial scope is text-only decoder models with one homogeneous full-attention KV group, on NVIDIA GPUs with the `FLASH_ATTN` or `TRITON_ATTN` attention backend, and on AMD ROCm GPUs with `TRITON_ATTN`: replace the `--attention-config` above with `--attention-config '{"backend":"TRITON_ATTN"}'`. On ROCm, Uno has been tested on the Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201); `TRITON_ATTN` on NVIDIA has been tested on one RTX 3090 (sm_86). Every other attention backend, FlashInfer included, is refused at startup; on both platforms the backend must be set explicitly. Model Runner V2 and async scheduling are required. Tensor parallelism is supported and the draft uses the target's `tensor_parallel_size`.
+
+User LoRA adapters are not supported yet: `--enable-lora` serves only Uno's own adapter. Python's `InputProcessor` refuses request adapters before queueing, and runtime LoRA loading is refused at startup. Prebuilt `EngineCoreRequest`s and frontends that bypass `InputProcessor`, including the Rust frontend, do not receive that refusal. Uno wraps the runner-owned manager's `set_active_adapters` method so bypass requests select their own target adapter even if its ID collides with Uno's adapter; the draft pass continues to use Uno's adapter.
+
+Pipeline/data/context parallelism, expert load balancing (EPLB), elastic expert parallelism, MLA, chunked-local, static-sink, reference sliding-window (R-SWA), sliding or hybrid attention, dynamic speculation depth, adaptive verification, KV transfer/offloading, `--kv-sharing-fast-prefill` and dual batch overlap are unsupported. Before target weights load, admission checks `enable_eplb`, `enable_elastic_ep`, `use_mla`, `attention_chunk_size`, normalized `ModelConfig.rswa_window`, positive `hf_text_config.param_sink_number`, `is_hybrid`, `is_attention_free` and `sliding_window` through `get_sliding_window()`.
+
+Uno's admission helper does not directly read `local_layer_ids`, `sliding_window_size`, `interleaved_sliding_window`, `sliding_windows`, `sparse_config` or `is_causal` before weights. Inkling sconv/SWA, those per-layer sliding layouts, sparse Step5 and DeepSeekV2 `is_causal=False` can require layer construction; `use_mla` can already be false for `is_causal=False`. Uno checks the actual cached attention backends after weights load, then requires one homogeneous full-attention KV group and native draft metadata updates. The normalized `sliding_window` check does not cover every per-layer layout.
+
+The `attention_chunk_size` refusal is conservative: it also rejects a Llama4 configuration whose layers are all NoPE even when that layout would not construct chunked attention.
+
+Prefix caching and chunked prefill use the native scheduler. Draft sampling retains raw logits by persistent request slot for native probabilistic rejection sampling. Uno uses native full CUDA graphs for drafting when the target graph mode and attention backend support uniform decode capture; a draft decode graph exists only when some `cudagraph_capture_sizes` entry is at most `max_num_seqs * K`, so small products (for example `K=1` with few sequences) draft eagerly. `--enforce-eager` disables graphs.
+
+The native `VLLM_LORA_ENABLE_DUAL_STREAM=1` option can overlap base and LoRA linear work. Measure it on the intended hardware and workload. Uno routes its draft rows through its adapter with the same LoRA mapping call the runner uses for target steps, so each draft pass and the following target step rebuild the native LoRA metadata, which waits on the host once per pass.
+
+At the context boundary, unused draft rows have clamped positions and no KV writes. Native scheduling and verification limit the usable candidates to the remaining context.

+    (request,) = create_requests(num_requests=1, num_tokens=1, block_size=4)
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+    manager = scheduler.kv_cache_manager
+
+    output = scheduler.schedule()
+    if num_available_blocks == 1:
+        assert not output.num_scheduled_tokens
+        assert request.status == RequestStatus.WAITING
+        assert not manager.get_blocks(request.request_id).blocks[0]
+        assert manager.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks() == num_available_blocks
+    else:
+        assert output.num_scheduled_tokens == {request.request_id: 1}
+        assert not output.scheduled_spec_decode_tokens
+        assert len(manager.get_block_ids(request.request_id)[0]) == 2
+        assert manager.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks() == 0
+
+    scheduler.finish_requests(request.request_id, RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED)
+    assert manager.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks() == num_available_blocks
+
+
+def test_speculative_context_limit_uses_the_scheduler_spec_token_cap(
+    uno_scheduler_factory,
+):
+    """Upstream contract: speculative scheduling respects max_model_len.
+
+    The scheduler already trims a request's scheduled drafts so its input
+    positions stay below max_model_len, and allocate_slots caps Uno's K
+    lookahead slots there; the drafter writes PAD slots past the limit (see
+    test_draft_does_not_write_null_or_unallocated_or_out_of_context_slots).
+    Accept every draft so the request leaps K + 1 tokens per step, and check
+    that no step schedules or allocates past the limit.
+    """
+    k, block_size, max_model_len = 4, 4, 18
+    scheduler = uno_scheduler_factory(
+        num_speculative_tokens=k,
+        block_size=block_size,
+        max_model_len=max_model_len,
+        num_blocks=16,
+    )
+    (request,) = create_requests(
+        num_requests=1, num_tokens=3, max_tokens=100, block_size=block_size
+    )
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+    rid = request.request_id
+    manager = scheduler.kv_cache_manager
+    max_blocks = -(-max_model_len // block_size)
+
+    scheduled_drafts = []
+    next_token = 100
+    output = scheduler.schedule()
+    for _ in range(max_model_len):
+        assert request.num_computed_tokens <= max_model_len - 1
+        assert len(manager.get_block_ids(rid)[0]) <= max_blocks
+        drafts = output.scheduled_spec_decode_tokens.get(rid, [])
+        scheduled_drafts.append(len(drafts))
+        sampled = list(drafts) + [next_token]
+        next_token += 1
+        _model_output(scheduler, output, [sampled])
+        if request.is_finished():
+            break
+        scheduler.update_draft_token_ids(
+            DraftTokenIds([rid], [list(range(next_token, next_token + k))])
+        )
+        next_token += k
+        output = scheduler.schedule()
+
+    assert request.status == RequestStatus.FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED
+    assert request.num_tokens == max_model_len
+    # Full drafts while there is room, then the existing cap trims the last.
+    assert scheduled_drafts == [0, k, k, k - 1]
+
+
+def test_uno_new_query_slots_reduce_the_scheduled_token_budget(uno_scheduler_factory):
+    """Each admitted Uno request reserves K-1 draft query slots."""
+    scheduler = uno_scheduler_factory(
+        max_num_seqs=2, max_num_batched_tokens=20, num_blocks=32
+    )
+    for request in create_requests(num_requests=2, num_tokens=10, block_size=4):
+        scheduler.add_request(request)
+
+    assert scheduler.schedule().num_scheduled_tokens == {"0": 10, "1": 4}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_accepted", [0, 3, 4])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("preempt", [False, True])
+def test_uno_verification_rolls_back_and_releases_suffix(
+    uno_scheduler_factory, num_accepted, preempt
+):
+    """K+1 verification commits accepted tokens and frees temporary KV on exit."""
+    scheduler = uno_scheduler_factory(num_blocks=9)
+    (request,) = create_requests(num_requests=1, num_tokens=3, block_size=4)
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+    rid = request.request_id
+    manager = scheduler.kv_cache_manager
+    initial_free_blocks = manager.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks()
+
+    def update(output, token_ids):
+        scheduler.update_from_output(
+            output,
+            ModelRunnerOutput(
+                req_ids=[rid],
+                req_id_to_index={rid: 0},
+                sampled_token_ids=[token_ids],
+                logprobs=None,
+                prompt_logprobs_dict={},
+                pooler_output=[],
+            ),
+        )
+
+    update(scheduler.schedule(), [10])
+    draft_ids = [11, 12, 13, 14]
+    scheduler.update_draft_token_ids(DraftTokenIds([rid], [draft_ids]))
+    output = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert output.num_scheduled_tokens == {rid: 5}
+    assert output.scheduled_spec_decode_tokens == {rid: draft_ids}
+    assert len(manager.get_block_ids(rid)[0]) == 3
+
+    accepted_ids = draft_ids[:num_accepted] + [20]
+    update(output, accepted_ids)
+    assert list(request.output_token_ids) == [10] + accepted_ids
+    assert request.num_computed_tokens == 4 + num_accepted
+    assert request.num_tokens == request.num_computed_tokens + 1
+
+    if preempt:
+        scheduler.update_draft_token_ids(DraftTokenIds([rid], [[21, 22, 23, 24]]))
+        scheduler.running.remove(request)
+        scheduler._preempt_request(request, 0.0)
+        assert request.status == RequestStatus.PREEMPTED
+        assert request.num_computed_tokens == 0
+        assert not request.spec_token_ids
+        assert not manager.get_blocks(rid).blocks[0]
+        assert manager.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks() == initial_free_blocks
+        resumed = scheduler.schedule()
+        assert resumed.num_scheduled_tokens == {rid: request.num_tokens}
+        assert not resumed.scheduled_spec_decode_tokens
+
+    scheduler.finish_requests(rid, RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED)
+    assert not manager.get_blocks(rid).blocks[0]
+    assert manager.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks() == initial_free_blocks
+
